chunks: [His Attributes in the Qur'an] Then look, O questioner:
Whatever of His attributes the Qur'an indicated to you, follow it and seek light from the radiance of its guidance,

and that knowledge which Satan prompted you to seek, which is neither obligatory upon you from the Book, nor is there any trace of it in the Sunnah of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and the Imams of guidance,
leave its knowledge to Allah, Glory be to Him, for that is the utmost limit of Allah's claim upon you.
And know that those firm in knowledge are those whom it sufficed from breaching the barriers erected against the unseen matters,
their acknowledgment of the general fact that they do not know the interpretation of the veiled unseen,
so Allah (Exalted) praised their admission of inability to grasp what they did not encompass with knowledge,
and He called their leaving deep investigation into what He did not obligate them to search for its essence, firmness.
So confine yourself to that, and do not measure the Greatness of Allah, Glory be to Him, according to the measure of your intellect, lest you be among the destroyed.
ai.seo_question: How should one distinguish between necessary knowledge of God and speculative knowledge in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This passage articulates the Shia doctrine of *Tawqif* (divine specification) in theology, distinguishing between attributes known through revelation (*Sunnah*) and those beyond human capacity (*Ghayb al-Mahjub*). It highlights the scholarly virtue of *Rasikhun fi al-Ilm*—those firmly grounded in knowledge—who avoid speculative excess by acknowledging the limits of their intellect, thereby preventing the error of measuring the Divine Essence against human reasoning.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [Attributes of Allāh as described in the Holy Qur’ān] Then look on questioner,
be confined to those of His attributes which the Qur’ān has described and seek light from the effulgence of its guidance.

Leave to Allāh that knowledge which Satan has prompted you to seek and which neither the Qur’ān enjoins you to seek nor is there any trace of it in the actions or sayings of the Prophet and other leaders (A'immah) of guidance.
This is the extreme limit of Allāh’s claim upon you.
Know that firm in knowledge are those who refrain from opening the curtains that lie against the unknown,
and their acknowledgement of ignorance about the details of the hidden unknown prevents them from further probe.
Allāh praises them for their admission that they are unable to get knowledge not allowed to them.
They do not go deep into the discussion of what is not enjoined upon them about knowing Him and they call it firmness.
Be content with this and do not limit the Greatness of Allāh after the measure of your own intelligence, or else you would be among the destroyed ones.
